what_could_not_be_done: The full 0-500 frame dense walk (every frame) was NOT run in both arms end to end -- gl.readPixels-class readback cost was measured directly this session at ~11.1s/grab (223s wall / 20 grabs, timing-probe-G1 at contention ~2.15-2.3/core -- better than the predecessor's 3.0-3.4/core but still the dominant cost). A full 500-frame walk at 2 grabs/frame plus periodic reference grabs is >3h/arm at that rate, which is not a turn-safe budget (HAZARDS SS13). Instead: fast-forwarded (stepFrames, unmeasured, cost-free) to frame 270 and measured DENSELY (every single frame, per-frame, not sub-sampled) from frame 270 to 450 -- the window bracketing the verdict's own sparse-sampled crash (2.3% at f240, 0.5% at f300, 0.0% at f360, 6.1% at f420; W1-FIRST-TEN-MINUTES-r1.md SS5) with 30-frame margin on both sides. This is a bounded window, not the full walk; if the true run extends outside [270,450] this measurement will not see it, and that is stated as a limitation, not hidden.
Did not re-diagnose or re-implement the vegetation-occlusion fix -- it is already on this branch (see below) and was not authored by this task.

key_finding_1_the_diagnostic_question_th.question: What collider set does the spring arm actually test against, and why is vegetation absent from it?
key_finding_1_the_diagnostic_question_th.answer: game/src/sim/camera.js#stepCamera (line 429) reads cell = sim.cell || EMPTY_CELL, and solveArm() (line 841) calls cell.sphereCast(...) against exactly that cell -- nothing else. sim.cell is assigned in game/src/engine.js from exactly two sources: (a) this._interiorCell, built by _syncInteriorCollisionCell() from interiorCollisionShapes(rec) -- an interior room's own shell; or (b) a settlement cell built at engine.js ~7034-7039 as `new CollisionCell('settlement:'+id, pv.settlementSolidsNear(x,z,45).shapes, ...)`, i.e. the output of game/src/render/exterior.js#settlementSolids() (line 3045), which is building walls/shells only by its own header comment. Grepped game/src exhaustively: no code path anywhere feeds canopy/trunk/tree placements into a CollisionCell's shapes array. Vegetation instead lives entirely in game/src/world/province.js as InstancedMesh crown/trunk pairs tracked via _registerOccludable()/updateOcclusion(), which only ever toggles rendering .visible flags -- it has no interaction with sim.cell, solveArm(), or sphereCast at all. That is the whole answer to 'why is vegetation absent': it was never wired into the arm's collider set in the first place, by construction, not by a bug in the set-membership test. This is why arm_len read 3.993 m (full extension) and arm_hit:false at the exact frame the player vanished (verdict SS5) -- the arm's own sphere-cast worked exactly as designed against exactly the set it owns; a tree was never a candidate member of it.

key_finding_2_a_fix_of_the_correct_categ.when: 2026-08-14T11:20:09Z (about 80 minutes after the verdict's evidence was captured at 10:02, and an ancestor of this task's pinned base 725bca6f)
key_finding_2_a_fix_of_the_correct_categ.what_it_does: Rewrote Province.prototype.updateOcclusion (game/src/world/province.js) from a proximity-BUBBLE-around-instance-ORIGIN test to a camera-to-actor SEGMENT test against each canopy instance's baked crown/trunk radius (_registerOccludable, _occluderRadiusM). This matches the verdict's own prescribed remedy ('the fix belongs in vegetation collision or a near-field occluder fade, not in deck undersides') -- it is the near-field-occluder-fade branch, not the arm-collision branch, which is consistent with finding 1: the arm cannot be the fix surface here.
key_finding_2_a_fix_of_the_correct_categ.the_flag_that_makes_it_a_ready_delete_th: Province.occlusionSightline (public, documented in the source as the control arm: 'set it to false and the behaviour is bit-for-bit the behaviour of the commit before this one'). Since updateOcclusion never touches sim.cell/solveArm, arm_len and arm_hit are provably identical whether this flag is on or off -- so a run-length regression measured with it off cannot be a disguised 'the arm just moved' explanation; the only thing that changes between the two arms is which InstancedMesh entries are hidden.
key_finding_2_a_fix_of_the_correct_categ.existing_check: tools/visual/occlusion-sightline-check.mjs exercises the shipped method against a synthetic one-tree scene (3 arms: the tree that defeats the old bubble, a trunk the old bubble already caught, a tree that must stay visible) and PASSES at HEAD as of this session. It does NOT measure a player_occluded run on the real walk -- that gap is what this task was dispatched to close, and remains open per the blockers above.
key_finding_2_a_fix_of_the_correct_categ.not_yet_done: No one has re-run RI-CAM01's own SS C.1 bar (longest player_occluded run, dense sampling) against this fix. That is the actual acceptance number and it has not been produced, before or after b476b55d, by anyone -- the verdict's 2/10 score and 'automatic fail' predate the fix and have not been re-judged since.

Even with that fix, gl.readPixels itself measured 10-20s per call under this session's contention -- budget accordingly or wait for contention.mjs to show a materially lower load before running the full walk.
